title: Constant generic rank affine module becomes free on blowup charts
statement: Let $R\to B$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Assume that for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and every field extension $K/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, the ring $B\otimes_R K$ is an integral domain. Let $h\in R$, let $r\geq0$ be an integer, and let $N$ be a finitely generated $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] with $N_h$ finitely presented over $B_h$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module, def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. For a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, let $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}$ be the inverse image of the zero prime of $B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, where residue fields and spectra are as in [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume $N_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}}\cong B_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}}^{\oplus r}$ whenever $h\notin\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Then there is a finitely generated ideal $I\subset R$ with $V(I)=V(h)$ such that the following holds for every $a\in I$. Put $R_a^I=R[I/a]\subset R[1/a]$, the subring generated by the image of $R$ and all $i/a$ for $i\in I$, put $B_a^I=B\otimes_R R_a^I$, and put $N_a^I=(N\otimes_R R_a^I)/T_a$, where $T_a=\{m\mid a^n m=0\text{ for some }n\geq0\}$. For every prime $\mathfrak p^{\prime}\subset R_a^I$, there is $g\in B_a^I$ whose image in $B_a^I\otimes_{R_a^I}\kappa(\mathfrak p^{\prime})$ is nonzero and for which $(N_a^I)_g\cong((B_a^I)_g)^{\oplus r}$.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space. Here the prime is written explicitly as the inverse image of the generic fibre prime.

proof.text: Choose a surjection $v:B^n\twoheadrightarrow N$. The kernel of $v_h$ is finitely generated: take a finite presentation $B_h^t\xrightarrow A B_h^m\xrightarrow w N_h\to0$ from [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], and lift $v_h$ and $w$ to maps $u:B_h^n\to B_h^m$ and $z:B_h^m\to B_h^n$ with $wu=v_h$ and $v_hz=w$. Then $\ker(v_h)$ is generated by the columns of $zA$ and $1-zu$: for $x\in\ker(v_h)$ write $ux=Ay$ and $x=zAy+(1-zu)x$. Clear denominators, including powers of $h$ needed to make their images under $v$ zero, obtaining a finitely generated $K\subset\ker v$ with $K_h=\ker(v_h)$. Set $M=B^n/K$. Thus $M$ is finitely presented, maps onto $N$, and $M_h=N_h$.

By [lem-trf-affine-geometrically-integral-projective], choose a split embedding $i:B\to F=\bigoplus_\alpha R$ with retraction $\rho$. Put $J=\operatorname{Fit}_r(M)$, using [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change]. A finite presentation makes $J$ finitely generated by finitely many minors. Choose generators $j_1,\ldots,j_t$, and let $C\subset R$ be generated by their finitely many coordinates in $F$. It is also the ideal of coordinates of all of $J$: for $b\in B$, the $R$-linear endomorphism $i\circ(b\cdot-)\circ\rho$ of $F$ expresses every coordinate of $bj_l$ as an $R$-linear combination of coordinates of $j_l$. Set $I=hC$.

For a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, flatness [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] makes $B/\mathfrak pB$ flat over the domain $R/\mathfrak p$, hence injective into its localization $B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$: tensor the injections given by multiplication by nonzero elements of $R/\mathfrak p$. Thus $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak pB$ is prime. If $h\notin\mathfrak p$, then $M_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}}$ is free of rank $r$. The minors definition and base-change clause of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] give $J B_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}}=B_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}}$. Some $j_l$ therefore avoids $\mathfrak pB$, so its split coordinates are not all in $\mathfrak p$. Hence $C\not\subset\mathfrak p$. Together with $I\subset(h)$ this proves $V(I)=V(h)$.

Fix $a\in I$; write $a=hc$ with $c\in C$, and set $R^*=R[I/a]$, $B^*=B\otimes_RR^*$ using [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Multiplication by $a$ on $R^*$ is injective by [lemma-nagata-chart-generator-regular], so multiplication by $h$ and by $c$ is injective as well. By [lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal], $hCR^*=aR^*=hcR^*$; cancelling $h$ gives $CR^*=cR^*$. The zero chart has no primes and can be discarded. Flatness of $B^*$ over $R^*$ follows from [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] by the tensor identity $L\otimes_{R^*}B^*=L\otimes_RB$; in particular $a$ and $c$ also act injectively on $B^*$.

Write $i(j_l)=\sum_\alpha d_{l\alpha}e_\alpha$. In $R^*$ write $d_{l\alpha}=c d^*_{l\alpha}$ and define $u_l=\rho(\sum_\alpha d^*_{l\alpha}e_\alpha)$ after base change. Then $j_l=cu_l$. Moreover $i(u_l)=\sum_\alpha d^*_{l\alpha}e_\alpha$: multiply this equality by $c$, use $i\rho i=i$, and cancel $c$ in the free module. Since the $d_{l\alpha}$ generate $CR^*=cR^*$, cancellation also shows that the $d^*_{l\alpha}$ generate $R^*$. For every prime $\mathfrak p^*\subset R^*$, some $u_l$ therefore avoids $\mathfrak p^*B^*$, since its coordinate avoids $\mathfrak p^*$. The fibre at $\mathfrak p^*$ is a domain by the geometric-integrality hypothesis; the flatness argument of step 3 shows that $\mathfrak q^*=\mathfrak p^*B^*$ is prime. Consequently $JB^*_{\mathfrak q^*}=(c)$. This uses just the split maps and the ideal equality proved in steps 2 and 4.

Put $P=M\otimes_RR^*$ and $M^*=P/(a\text{-power torsion})$. By [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], $\operatorname{Fit}_r(P_{\mathfrak q^*})=(c)$. Apply [lem-trf-affine-principal-fitting-generators] to the finite module $P_{\mathfrak q^*}$ over the local ring $B^*_{\mathfrak q^*}$. Its quotient by $\ker(c)$ has at most $r$ generators. The module $M^*_{\mathfrak q^*}$ is a quotient of this module, since $cx=0$ implies $ax=hcx=0$; localization of the power-torsion quotient has exactly the localized power torsion, by clearing the extra denominator. Thus $M^*_{\mathfrak q^*}$ has at most $r$ generators. No equality between the Fitting ideals of $P$ and $M^*$ is asserted.

Choose $r$ elements of $M^*$ representing these localized generators, clearing their denominators (and padding by zero if necessary). The cokernel of $(B^*)^r\to M^*$ is finite, and its localization at $\mathfrak q^*$ is zero. For each member of a finite generating family choose an annihilator outside $\mathfrak q^*$, and multiply these annihilators. The resulting $g\notin\mathfrak q^*$ makes $(B^*_g)^r\to M^*_g$ surjective. For $r=0$ this already proves the required freeness; the following lower-Fitting argument is needed only for $r>0$.

Assume $r>0$ and put $L=\operatorname{Fit}_{r-1}(M)$. At each fibre-generic prime over $R_h$, the rank-$r$ free-module hypothesis makes $L$ zero after localization, by the minors definition and localization clause of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change]. Apply [lem-trf-affine-generic-localization-intersection] to $R_h\to B_h$: flatness, finite presentation and geometric integrality persist under this localization, and its fibre-generic primes are precisely the original ones with $h\notin\mathfrak p$. The injective product map therefore gives $L B_h=0$.

Set $L^*=\operatorname{Fit}_{r-1}(M^*)$. The chart satisfies $(R^*)_a=R_a$, since its generators $i/a$ already lie in $R_a$. Also $h$ is invertible in $R_a$, with inverse $c/a$ since $a=hc$. Thus $M^*_a=P_a$ and step 8, together with [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], gives $L^*B^*_a=0$. Every element of $L^*$ is consequently killed by some power of $a$; the injectivity of multiplication by $a$ on $B^*$ from step 4 yields $L^*=0$. In the surjection $(B^*_g)^r\to M^*_g$ of step 7, the $(r-1)$st Fitting ideal is exactly the ideal of entries of all kernel vectors (the minors have size one). By [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] this ideal is zero, so every kernel vector is zero and the surjection is an isomorphism.

Finally $M\twoheadrightarrow N$ induces a surjection $M^*\twoheadrightarrow N^*$. It becomes an isomorphism after inverting $a$, since $h$ is then invertible and $M_h=N_h$. Each element of its kernel is therefore killed by a power of $a$, while multiplication by $a$ on $M^*$ is injective by its defining power-torsion quotient: if $ax$ is power torsion then so is $x$. Hence the kernel is zero. The free open from steps 7--9 transfers to $N^*$. Because $g\notin\mathfrak p^*B^*$, its image in the domain fibre is nonzero by the injection proved as in step 3. This proves every clause for the original finite module $N$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q35-e8b659f80 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery against Stacks Tag 0810 (flat.tex, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space), Tag 05FT, Tag 080Z (more-algebra) and Tag 05DH. The item statement matches 0810 hypothesis by hypothesis and was not changed. q_p=pB follows from flatness, and 'nonzero in the fibre' is equivalent to g not in p'S'. I checked all 10 steps: the kernel generators zA and 1-zu, the coordinate ideal C (using the endomorphism i∘(b·)∘ρ), V(I)=V(h), cancelling h to get CR*=cR*, the divided coordinates generating the unit ideal, 080Z applied locally with ker(c) inside the a-power torsion, spreading the generators out, Fit_{r-1} vanishing through the new injection node and regularity of a, and the transfer back to N. Both corrections to the source are right: (1) R'_a=R_f fails, for example R=k[x,y], I=(x), a=xy gives R'=R[1/y]; (2) the divided generator need not be a unit, for example R=k, B=k[x], J=(x). All three new nodes are true, give only a statement, introduce their own objects, are not duplicates (rg found no node for 05FT, 080Z or 05DH; lem-trf-free-subtraction-flatness and the two pbc localization-injectivity nodes state different things) and do not restate a clause of the item. Mathlib has no Fitting ideals. I accepted the Nagata chart lemmas as tool uses. Nothing cites SGA. I made no changes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_affine_generic_rank_blowup (R : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] (N : ModuleCat.{w} B) (hflat : RingHom.Flat (algebraMap R B)) [Algebra.FinitePresentation R B] [Module.Finite B N] (h : R) (r : ℕ) (hfp : Module.FinitePresentation (Localization.Away (algebraMap R B h)) (LocalizedModule.Away (algebraMap R B h) N)) (hgeom : ∀ (p : PrimeSpectrum R) (K : Type (max u v w)) [Field K] [Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)) K] [Algebra R K] [IsScalarTower R (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)) K], IsDomain (B ⊗[R] K)) (hfree : ∀ (p : PrimeSpectrum R) (q : PrimeSpectrum B), q.asIdeal = RingHom.ker (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : B →ₐ[R] p.asIdeal.Fiber B).toRingHom → h ∉ p.asIdeal → Nonempty (LocalizedModule.AtPrime q.asIdeal N ≃ₗ[Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal] (Fin r → Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))) : ∃ I : Ideal R, I.FG ∧ I.radical = (Ideal.span {h}).radical ∧ ∀ (a : R), a ∈ I → ∀ p' : PrimeSpectrum (AffineBlowup.chartRing I a : Type u), ∃ g : affineGenericRankChartAlgebra R B I a, g ∉ p'.asIdeal.map (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := B) (B := (AffineBlowup.chartRing I a : Type u))).toRingHom ∧ Nonempty (LocalizedModule.Away g (affineGenericRankChartModule R B N I a) ≃ₗ[Localization.Away g] (Fin r → Localization.Away g))
lean.note: The two helper declarations construct only the chart algebra and module explicitly introduced in this node, using the existing chartRing and powTorsion notions. The generic-prime kernel equality specifies exactly the inverse image of the zero prime. Radical equality is equivalent to equality of vanishing sets; the nonzero fibre-image clause is equivalently g outside the extended base prime, by flatness. No statement correction is made. Maintainer convention repair: the generic-fibre map now uses Mathlib Ideal.Fiber and its canonical includeRight; tensor symmetry identifies its kernel with the delivered includeLeft kernel. No mathematical statement change.
